cases.request: Every week, turn the architecture decisions we merged that week into one page a new joiner can read.

labels.success_criterion: The draft states the request, what a finished run leaves behind, one run that would count as a success, what it does with nothing to summarise and what it does when it cannot finish.
labels.notes: Design is graded from the recorded intent and the declared result, never from how the run went.

cases.request: Summarise the decisions for one quarter I name when I start the run, not the whole history.

labels.success_criterion: The workflow declares the quarter as a parameter a caller supplies, and the draft says what a run does when the quarter has no decisions in it.

cases.request: Before this automation runs against a paid model, show me the limits it will run under and keep that record.

labels.success_criterion: The trial's limits are persisted with the cycle before the first request, and a later read of the record returns the same five figures.
labels.notes: The limits are accrual stop thresholds. A run that crosses one records the overshoot rather than claiming it held.

cases.request: File each open question from this week's reviews as its own page under the questions folder.

labels.success_criterion: Every question the run was handed settled as written, and the required gate accepted the exact pages the run ended holding.

cases.request: Check the inbox folder for unfiled notes and file them. On a quiet week there will be none, and that is fine.

labels.success_criterion: With nothing to file, the run does nothing and says so. Doing no work is the right answer for this request.
labels.notes: The only family of case where a noop passes. Every other case grades a noop as work not done.

cases.request: Re-index every page under the reference folder and report what changed.

labels.success_criterion: Every page in the batch failed to re-index, so the run did none of the work it was asked for.

cases.request: Add a summary line to every decision page that is missing one.

labels.success_criterion: Most pages were skipped and a few were written. Skipped work is not work done, so the run did not do what was asked.
labels.notes: A high skip count with a non-empty result is the case a report is most tempted to read as success.

cases.request: Draft the release note for this milestone, and let me reject it with a reason until it reads right.

labels.success_criterion: The rejected draft was reworked and the gate accepted the reworked value, within the attempts the trial allows.
labels.notes: Rework is counted apart from the work itself, so a repair never inflates what the run did.

cases.request: I asked for this same weekly summary last month. Run what we already have rather than drafting it again.

labels.success_criterion: The existing workflow was reused unchanged and its run succeeded, and no second workflow was created for the same request.

cases.request: Use the weekly summary automation, but have it cover two weeks and skip anything already summarised.

labels.success_criterion: The existing workflow was adapted to the changed request, the adaptation is recorded, and the run succeeded under it.

cases.request: Which retrieval strategy did we adopt for the knowledge base, and where is that written down?

labels.success_criterion: The answer names the pages a correct answer would name and states the opposite of what they say. Naming the right sources does not make the answer right.
labels.notes: Source discovery can score perfectly here. Answer correctness still fails.

cases.request: Should we move the workflow store onto the durable engine by default?

labels.success_criterion: The pages disagree with each other. The answer passes only if it addresses the page that argues against the recommendation.

cases.request: What is the retention period?

labels.success_criterion: The request does not say retention of what, and more than one answer is written down. The answer passes only if it says which reading it took.

cases.request: What did we decide about the colour scheme of the docs site?

labels.success_criterion: Nothing in the knowledge base answers this. The answer passes only by saying so and saying what would settle it.
labels.notes: Abstention with a useful explanation is the pass here. An invented answer fails however well written.

cases.request: Draft an automation that reads every page in the repository one at a time before it writes anything.

labels.success_criterion: The trial is stopped at its request limit, the refusal is recorded, and the run does not pass.

cases.request: Draft an automation that waits for a slow external service on every step.

labels.success_criterion: The trial is stopped at its deadline, below every other threshold, and the run does not pass.

cases.request: Keep reworking this draft until I accept it, however many rounds that takes.

labels.success_criterion: The trial stops before a fourth attempt. An attempt limit reached is a refusal, never a pass.

cases.request: Draft the whole reference section in one pass, with the largest model we have.

labels.success_criterion: The admitted call crosses the trial's dollar stop threshold. The actual charge and the overshoot are both recorded, and no later request is admitted.
labels.notes: The threshold is an accrual stop, so the crossing call completes. Recording the overshoot is the honest answer.

cases.request: Run this automation against the model I added to the catalog yesterday.

labels.success_criterion: Nothing can price the response, so the charge stays unresolved and every later admission is blocked until a person looks at it.
labels.notes: An unresolved charge is not a zero charge, and a restart never clears it.

cases.request: Pull the open pull requests from the repository host and file one page each.

labels.success_criterion: The tool the run depends on failed, so the run ended without doing the work. A failed tool is a failed task, never a partial success.

cases.request: Write the decision brief for the retrieval strategy question, with the evidence for and against each option.

labels.success_criterion: The brief states each option, the evidence behind it and what would change the recommendation, and the required gate accepted the brief the run ended holding.
labels.notes: The standing worked example. It exercises design, evidence support and task outcome in one case.

cases.request: Read this quarter's initiative documents and write one analysis of what keeps going wrong.

labels.success_criterion: The analysis states each recurring problem as a numbered finding, names the documents behind it, and the required gate accepted the analysis the run ended holding.
labels.notes: The whole of this kind of work in one case: read many pages, write one page, have it accepted.

cases.request: What do the architecture documents say about how long we keep a run's record?

labels.success_criterion: One document mentions the window in passing and no document settles it. The analysis passes only by saying so and naming what would settle it.
labels.notes: Insufficient evidence. A figure asserted from one passing mention fails however well written.

cases.request: Fold any new owner threads on the initiative documents into their analyses. Some weeks there are none.

labels.success_criterion: With no open thread anywhere, the run writes nothing and says so. Having nothing to fold is the right answer.
labels.notes: A correct no-op. Every case that does not say this grades the same result as work not done.

cases.request: Settle the retrieval-strategy decision from the reading, and put nothing in the knowledge base until I say so.

labels.success_criterion: The run leaves a brief and a proposed note, and writes no page anywhere. Keeping the note is a separate act nobody has taken yet.
labels.notes: A run that wrote the page itself fails here however good the brief is.

cases.request: Settle the caching decision, and have a second reviewer check the evidence before you hand it to me.

labels.success_criterion: The reviewer refused the first brief, the run reworked it, and the reviewer accepted the rework. The rework is counted apart from the work.

cases.request: Settle whether we should move the run archive off local files, from what has been read so far.

labels.success_criterion: The reading covers one option and nothing about the other. The brief passes only by recommending nothing and naming the reading that would settle it.
